rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CAR COMPANIES TO PUT UP SUB-ASSEMBLY PLANTS FOR THE LOCAL MANUFACTURE OF CERTAIN CAR OR AUTO PARTS
rows.abstract: Car manufacturing is undubtedly a profitable industry raking millions of millions in profits. However, since the motoring public buy their car or auto parts at prices that are not well within their financial capacity, the author of this bill envisions that if the car companies could be indeed be required to set up sub-assembly lines with the use of local raw materials and local labor, then it will not only generate employment opportunities but it will significantly lower the prices of these caror auto parts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT ADOPTING A COMPUTERIZED SYSTEM OF ELECTION FOR THE 2004 GENERAL ELECTIONS AND SUBSEQUENT ELECTIONS, PLEBISCITES, REFERENDA, RECALL AND OTHER ELECTORAL EXERCISES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill substantiates the policy of the State to ensure free, orederly, honest, fair and credible elections and other electoral exercises, and ensure the secrecy and sanctity of the ballot in order that the citizenry shall be assured that the results of elections, plebiscites, referenda and such other electoral exercises are truly reflective of their will.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09189) enacted on 2003-02-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF ABSENTEE VOTING FOR QUALIFIED FILIPINOS ABROAD AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: All Filipinos abroad and their spouse and dependents when residing with them who have all the qualifications and none of the disqualificatio ns of a voter shall have the right to register and to vote by absentee ballot.> They shall include the following: 1) Contract workers employed in foreign countries; 2) Employees of the Philippine Government assigned in foreign countries; 3) Filipino citizens who are legally immigrants or temporary residents of foreign countries.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03570

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'ls as per J.16;p.33( Aug. 27,2001);j t. ref'ls as per J.17; p.25(Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF AND THE CONDUIT NETWORK FOR AGRI-AGRA CREDITS, PRESCRIBING A FIXED PERCENTAGE OF THE FUNDS FOR LENDING TO SMALL FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES THEREBY AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 717, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE AGRI-AGRA LAW
rows.abstract: This billl seeks to REDIRECT CREDIT to where it is direly needed. This proposed measure mandates that fifty percent (50%) of the twenty-five percent (25%) of a bank's total loanable funds reserved for agricultural and agrarian reform credits be extended to the small farmers and fisherfolk and their cooperatives. Moreover, it removes the provision in P>D> 717 which allows banks to divert to government securities the ten percent (10%) agrarian reform share aforecited. And for its strict compliance by the financial institutions, a penalty provision is included.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: change of cttee. ref'l from J.5; p.30 (July 31,2001)

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PUNISHING THE CRIME OF KIDNAPPING-FOR- RANSOM WITH AMPUTATION OF UPPER AND LOWER EXTREMITIES THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLE 267 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The perpetrators of kidnap-for-rans om should be dealt with punishments as severe as the crimes they commit against the lives, property, and rights under the Constitution. The crime of kidnapping-for- ransom is not as simple as taking a man in unlawful and illegitimate custody for the purpose of soliciting money in exchange for victim's freedom.  It has been proven to be viciously victimizing middle or the moneyed class in society.Let it stop and the psychological deterrent for its recurrence be to impose amputation of the upper and lower extremities(the punishment of such crime.) It is not intended to be a cruel and inhumane punishment, but only a consequence. As a matter of fact, giving the sentence of death a middle ground...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: change of ctte. ref'l from Justice as per Rules Instructio ns on July 25,2001

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CENTER FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDIES AND NATIONAL SECURITY DEVELOPMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Center shall primarily provide advance studies and progressive leadership in national security development and administration. It shall strengthen international relations and promote research and extension services in relevant fields.> The Center shall offer courses in the field of international studies and national security development and administration, and such courses as its governing body may deem necessary to carry out its objectives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ECOTOURISM POLICY, ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR ITS INSTITUTIONALIZ ATION, CREATING A MECHANISM FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes an ecotourism policy growth and environmental protection. It creates a National Ecotourism Commission which shall formulate and implement an Ecotourism Master Plan with the assistance of the Department of Tourism and the Department of Environment and Natural resources. The bill also proposes a network of ecotourism sites which would be inclided in the Integrated Areas System under R.A. No. 7586, also known as National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 1992 (NIPAS).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: ctte. ref'l as per Rules instructio n on 7/25/2001; jt. ref'l as per J.37; p.19

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT LEGALIZING JUETENG AND PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE LOTTERY CORPORATION OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposal is based on the following objectives: (1) To eliminate the corrupting influence of jueteng, especially on public officers; (2) To raise revenue for the government to be used for charitable purposes and programs intended to uplift the conditions of the "masa"; and (3) To formulate rules that shall safeguard the interest of the betting public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ROLE, DIRECT PARTICIPATION AND ACTIVE INVOLVEMENT OF THE COMMON PEOPLE THROUGH COOPERATIVES IN GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE CONTRACTS AND PROJECTS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This proposed measure is an attempt to renew our people's commitment to that battle cry by strengthening a concrete manifestation of people empowerment -- the COOPERATIVES.> Specifically, this bill endeavors to grant qualified cooperatives the chance to engage and/or participate in government infrastructure contracts and projects as a contractor. The author firmly believes that this will lead to a more equitable distribution of the fruits of development and further strengthen the democratic gains of our people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: as per Rules Instructio ns on July 25,2001;as per J.2;July 24,2001,p. 21

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO SET ASIDE AREAS FOR MANDATORY BAMBOO PLANTING AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All local government units are hereby required to set aside areas in their locality to be used for mandatory tree planting.> All persons, natural or juridical, applying for any permit or license in the said local government unit shall be required toplant bamboo in the areas hereby set aside.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROMOTION OF BIO-ORGANIC FARMING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Bio-organic farming is defined as a system of agricultural production which avoids the use of chemical or inorganic farm inputs, pesticides, weedicides and feed additives, and relies on biological means of conditioning and enriching the soil and of controlling pests.> It would be to the advantage of our environment , out economy and iltimately our people, to adopt this measure providing for the promotion of bio-organic farming in the Philippines.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04468

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF BARANGAY DRUGSTORES, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "BOTICA SA BARANGAY" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Drugstores are normally non-existent in barangays outside of the town proper. Most of our people in the countryside are thus deprived of access even to basic drugs and medicines when they are afflicted and in need.> Within a period of three (3) years, the Department of Health is enjoined to establish barangay drugstores or "botica sa barangay" in every barangay making available drugs for common illnesses such as fever, pain, cough/colds and others, including vitamin and mineral preparations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE WELFARE OF BARANGAY TANODS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to recognize and acknoeldge the sacrifices of our BARANGAY Tanod by providing them the same benefits as the other barangay officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C052
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09211) enacted on 2003-06-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING A SMOKE-FREE ENVIRONMENT BY REGULATING THE PRODUCTION, MANUFACTURE, LABELLING, ADVERTISEMENT AND SALE OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS, AND ESTABLISHING A TRUST FUND THEREOF
rows.abstract: "National Toabacco Control Act." This bill seeks to: (a) Regulate all tobacco advertisements; (b) Regulate tobacco products' labelling; (c) Prohibit the sale of tobacco products to minors; and (d) Create and establish a Trust Fund that will answer for the major programs of the government in line with this Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE LEGITIMATION OF CHILDREN BORN TO PARENTS BELOW MARRYING AGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Art. 177 of EO No. 209 (Family Code) is hereby AMENDED  to read as follows:> "Only children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other, EXCEPT BY IMPEDIMENT OF BEING UNDERAGED, may be legitimated."
rows.status: Substituted by HB04538

rows.author: C052
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING A 3-DAY NON-CUMULATIVE LEAVE WITH PAY ANNUALLY TO EMPLOYED PARENTS TO ATTEND TO THE SPECIAL NEEDS OF THEIR CHILDREN
rows.abstract: "Parental Leave Act of 2001."> Employees who are paretns or guardians, whether working in the public or private sector, shall be entitled to a parental leave of three (3) days annually with pay, to enable them to attend to special circumstances involving their children or wards in any school activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C052
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INSURANCE BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY TANODS PROVIDING FUNDS  FOR THE PAYMENT OF ITS PREMIUMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Barangay Tanod Insurance Act of 2001." In recognition of their services, barangay tanods, in addition to the benefits under existing laws, shall be entitled to the following benefits: (a) Free life insurance of P20,000.00; (b) Burial expenses of P10,000.00; (c) Free hospitalization /medical services up to P10,000.00 per year, provided, however, that the disease, illness or injury is contracted in the performance of their official uniform; and (d) Free legal services - legal representation andconsultation services for barangay tanods shall be immediately provided by the Public Attorneys Office in cases of coercion, interference, and in civil and criminal cases filed by or against barangay tanods arising out of or in conection with the perrformance of their official duties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C052
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS FOR BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS ONE THOUSAND PESOS PER MONTH, FOR THE PURPOSE OF AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7883
rows.abstract: In recongnition of their services, all accredited barangay health workers who are actively and regularly performing their duties shall be entitled to RECEIVE HONORARIUM IN THE AMOUNT OF ONE THOUSAND (P1,000.00) PESOS PER MONTH IN ADDITION TO THE INCENTIVES AND BENEFITS PROVIDED FOR BY LAW.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: MAGNA CARTA FOR CUSTOMS BROKER PROFESSION
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the national policy to give priority to attention to the pursuit of the Customs Broker profession, which will be beneficial to the country in general, and to the economy in particular. > The Government shall provide a program to setup a climate conducie to the practice of the profession, give encouragement and support to students who may want to pursue a career in customs brokerage or customs brokers or customs administration, and maximize the capability and potential of our Filipino customs brokers and the entire customs brokerage business through incentives and other forms of assistance and support.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05957

rows.author: C084
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EMPLOYERS IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR TO HAVE IN THEIR EMPLOY DISABLED PERSONS, AND PROVIDING ADDITIONAL INCENTIVE THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-TWO SEVENTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MAGNA CARTA FORDISABLED PERSONS
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to add the following provisions to RA No. 7277, the Magna Carta for Disabled Person:> EVERY EMPLOYER IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR SHALL ENSURE THAT AT LEAST THREE PERCENT (3%) OF HIS TOTAL REGULAR OR PERMANENT WORKFORCE,INCLU SIVE OF MANAGERIAL AND SUPERVISORIAL PERSONNEL, SHALL BE COMPOSED OF DISABLED PERSONS WHO SHALL HAVE QUALIFIED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PRECEDING SECTION. EMPLOYERS SHALL COMPLY WITH THE PROVISION OF THIS SECTION WITHIN ONE (1) YEAR FROM THE DATE OF EFFECTIVITY OFTHIS ACT. FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH THIS SECTIO SHALL BE PENALIZED IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 46, PARAGRAPH (A) OF THIS ACT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MEMBERSHIP OF DULY-ELECTED PRESIDENTS OF THE FEDERATION OF BARANGAY KAGAWADS IN THE MUNICIPAL, CITY AND PROVINCIAL SANGGUNIANS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 508 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: SANGGUNIAN MEMBERS OF BARANGAYS SHALL FORM A NATIONAL FEDERATION, WITH CHAPTERS AT THE MUNICIPAL, CITY, PROVINCIAL AND METROPOLITAN POLITICAL SUBDIVISION LEVELS, THE DULY ELECTED PRESIDENTS OF THE FEDERATION AT THE MUNICIPAL, CITY AND PROVINCIAL LEVEL, INCLUDING THE COMPONENT CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES OF METRO MANILA SHALL SERVE AS EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG BAYAN, SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD, AND SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN, RESPECTIVELY. THEY SHALL SERVE AS SUCH ONLY DURING THEIR TERM OF OFFICE AS PRESIDENTS OF THE FEDERATION CHAPTERS, WHICH IN NO CASE SHALL BE BEYOND THE TERM OF OFFICE OF THE SANGGUNIANG CONCERNED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT AND CONSTRUCTION OF AN EDUCATIONAL CENTER FOR SPECIAL CHILDREN IN THE FIRST DISTRICT OF PAMPANGA TO BE KNOWN AS APOLINARIO MABINI EDUCATIONAL CENTER FOR SPECIAL CHILDREN OF PAMPANGA, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF NON-FORMAL EDUCATION BY CREATING ITEMS FOR DISTRICT NON-FORMAL EDUCATION COORDINATORS AND TEACHERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The position of district NON-FORMAL EDUCATION COORDINATOR is hereby created in every school district in the Philippines. Elementary grade teachers who are actually designated and performing the duties and functions od a district non-formal educationcoordinator shall have the rank and privileges of an elementary school principal, subject to adjustments approved by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).
rows.status: Substituted by HB06033

rows.author: C064
rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE NATIONAL TELECOMMUNICATI ONS COMMISSION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seek sto create a more responsive public service delivery abreast with the times and taking into consideration the highly enhanced modern, and advanced communication and information technology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C064
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL CEBU CAMPUS IN ARGAO, CEBU, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C064
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-03-20, transmitted to on 2003-03-21 and received by the Senate on 2003-03-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE MANDATE ON THE INTERCONNECTION BETWEEN AND AMONG PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATI ONS ENTITIES, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (convergence)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Recognizing the vital role of teloecommunicat ions in nation-building and economic development, the State in its desire to attain universal access shall promote the rapid expandion of telecommunicati ons services in all areas of the Philippines, maximize the use of all available telecommunicati ons facilities, and ensure that every user of the public telecommunicati ons service shall have access to such facilities at a mandated standard of service and at reasonable costs.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04418

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING AN ADVANCED STUDIES DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR EXCEPTIONAL EMPLOYEES FROM THE GOVERNMENT AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Pensionado Act of 2001." This bill seeks to provide our country with a constant supply of highly trained leaders for industry, research and academe. In this proposed measure, the maximum utilization of returning scholars will be coordinated under a single governing body where all scholarships under foreign and local sponsorhip are pooled together.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR EDUCATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill aims to:  (1) to provide efficient ad effective government structures and machinery that shall consistently carry-out the implementation of education policies, plans and programs;  (2) formulate long-term goals and objectives and define strategic direction for a system-lelvel assessment on education at least every five (5) years; (3) make the educational system functionally linked with the other sectos of our society whose operation  and environment interact with or has impact on education; etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING BENEFITS TO DEPENDENTS OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AMENDING FOR THESE PURPOSES REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FORTY-SIX HUNDRED SEVENTY (REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4670), OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MAGNA CARTA FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Magna Carta for Public Schoolteachers had failed to provide benefits to the DEPENDENTS of teachers. Thus, this bill seeks to grant ADDITIONAL benefits to teachers by giving their dependents the right to scholarship grants, free medical treatment and pension in case of disability of the teachers. In addition, it also encourages teachers to form cooperatives in their own municipalities to help promote their economic welfare.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE THE TEACHING OF RELIGION IN THE PUBLIC SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: This proposed measure substantiates the State policy to encourage and promote the teaching of religion to children in public elementary and high schools within the regular class hours, cognizant of the vital role of the teaching of religion in citizen formation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TAX INCENTIVES TO BROADCAST AND PRINT MEDIA DEVOTING AIR TIME AND SPACE TO EDUCATION AS WELL AS TO SPONSORS SUPPORTING SUCH PROGRAMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Congnizant of the problem being encountered by the media industry and recognizing the importance of media to the present educational program, this bill grants tax incentives to media programs and publications, as well as to their respective advertisers and sponsors, with educational thrust. It is hoped that the measures contained in this bill will alleviate the economic plight of the media industry as a whole and shall become an effective tool in the success of the national educational program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE SUMMARY TITLING OF REAL PROPERTIES USED AS SITES FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: The bill aims to provide all lands being utilized as public sites with titles under the name of the Department of Education, Culture and Sports to enable it to have legal ownership over these school sites.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09208) enacted on 2003-05-26
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTE POLICIES TO ELIMINATE THE TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS ESPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS, ESTABLISHING THE NECESSARY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION AND SUPPORT OF TRAFFICKED PERSONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Trafficki ng Act of 2001." With this proposed measure, special recognition is given to the vulnerablity of women and minors and it shall afford special protection to them.> Specific measures will be instituted, not only to support trafficked persons, especially women and minors, but more importantly, to mitigate pressures for involuntary migration and servitude of persons especially women and minors.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04432

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXPAND THE EXCLUSIVE APPELLATE JURISDICTION OF THE COURT OF APPEALS TO INCLUDE LABOR CASES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 9 (3) OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 129, AS AMENDED, KNOWN AS THE JUDICIARY REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1980
rows.abstract: This bill extends the appellate jurisdiction of the Court of Appeals to the NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION, INCLUDING THE FINAL DECISIONS OF THE SECRETARY OF LABOR IN CERTIFICATION ELECTION CASES AND INTERNAL UNION CONFLICTS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 285 AND 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR AN EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA) TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract: The share of local government units in the internal revenue allotment shall be allocated [in the following manner:] BEGINNING IN 1996 AFTER DEDUCTING THERE FROM THE COSTS OF DEVOLUTION, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS GUARANTEED FUND. THE GUARANTEED FUND SHALL BE DISTRIBUTED AND REMITTED DIRECTLY TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS CONCERNED AND THE NET OR BALANCE OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT SHALL BE ALLOCATED IN THE FOLLOWING MANNER: (a) Provinces - Twenty-three percent (23%); (b) Cities - Twenty-three percent (23%); (c) Municipalities - [Thirty-four percent (34%))] THIRTY-PERCENT (30%); and (d) Barangays - Twenty percent (20%): Provided, however, That the share of each province, city and municipality shall be determined on the basis of the followingformula: (a) Population DENSITY -Fifty percent (50%); AND (b) [Land Area - Twenty-five percent (25%) and] POVERTY INCIDENCE - FIFTY PERCENT (50%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE STATUTORY PROVISION AUTHORIZING THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES TO MAKE NECESSARY ADJUSTMENT IN THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT INCURS AN UNMANAGEABLE PUBLIC SECTOR DEFICIT, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 284 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160
rows.title_short: Amending the Statutory Provision Authorizing the President to Adjust the Internal Revenue Allotment
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to protect the Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) share of the local government units from funding restrictions or holdback in the event that the national government incurs an unmanageable public sector deficit.> The local governments,being at the forefront in the delivery of essential services to the people must always be assured of local autonomy and financial viability as mandated by the Constitution and the Local Government Code.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-07, transmitted to on 2002-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-13

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL INSURANCE BENEFITS TO ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PAYMENT OF ITS PREMIUMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In addition to the existing insurance benefits given to public schoolteachers by the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) under Republic Act No. 8291, a term insurance coverage to all public schoolteachers providing the following benefits shall be granted: (a)  death benefits of Two Hundred Thousand (P200,000.00) to all teachers who are in active service; (b) burial expenses of Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) to all teachers who are in active service; and (c) reimbursement of actual medical expenses of all teachers, whether retired or in the active service, but not to exceed One HUndred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill provides for the establishment of a PUBLIC SCHOOLTEACHERS SCHOLARSHIP FUND. The grantee of the scholarship program under this Act shall be entitled to financial assistance which may include tuition and other school fees, outright grant forprescribed textbooks and essential school supplies, transportation assistance, and living allowance. Provided, however, that in the granting of financial assistance, the availability of funds, purchasing power of the peso and rate of financial assistance given udner other government scholarship programs must be considered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE AUTOMATIC RELEASE OF THE SHARE OF THE BARANGAY IN THE PROCEEDS OF NATIONAL TAXES AND TAXES ON THE UTILIZATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL WEALTH, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 286, CHAPTER 1 AND SECTION 293, CHAPTER 2, TITLE 3, BOOK II, RESPECTIVELY, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The share of each local government unit shall be released, without need of any further action, directly to the provincial, city, municipal or barangay treasurer, as the case may be, on a quarterly basis within five (5) days after the end of each quarter, and which shall not be subject to any lien or holdback that may be imposed by the National Government, AND LIKEWISE THE SHARE OF THE BARANGAYS SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO ANY LIEN OR HOLDBACK THAT MAY BE IMPOSED BY PROVINCIAL, CITY OR MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT, for whatever purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE TAX ON IDLE LANDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, SECTION 236 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: A province or city, of a municipality within the Metropolitan Manila, may levy an annual tax on idle lands at the rate not exceeding [five] (5%) TEN percent (10%) of the assessed value of the property which shall be in addition to the basic real property tax.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE AUTOMATIC HOLDING OF SPECIAL ELECTIONS WHENEVER A VACANCY OCCURS IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES , AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6645, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANNER OF FILLING A VACANCY IN THECONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES,' AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166
rows.abstract: This bill proposes the holding of special elections automatically whenever a vacancy occurs in the House of Representatives at least one (1) year before the next regular elections for Members of Congress, amending for the purpose Republic Act No. 6645.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION TWO HUNDRED TWENTY OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: THE REAL PROPERTY CLASSIFIED AS RESIDENTIAL SHALL NOT BE REASSESSED MORE OFTENER THAN ONCE EVERY TEN (10) YEARS, AND THAT EACH REASSESSMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED TWENTY PERCENT (20%) ON LAND A TEN PERCENT (10%) ON BUILDINGS AND OTHER STRUCTURES: AND PROVIDED, FINALLY, THAT IN CASE OF VIOLATION  OF THIS PROVISION, A PENALTY OF PERPETUAL DISQUALIFICATIO N  TO HOLD PUBLIC OFFICE OR A FINE OF NOT EXCEEDING THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (P300,000.00) OR BOTH DISQUALIFICATIO N AND FINE IN THE DISCRETION OFTHE COURT, SHALL BE IMPOSED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE REGISTRATION OF THE SALE OF PREPAID SUBSCRIBER IDENTITY MODULE (SIM) PACKS FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: All corporations, partnerships and single proprietorships engaged in the business of selling prepaid subscriber identity module (SIM) packs for cellular telephones are hereby required to cause the REGISTRATION of the following information in an official record-document established for the purpose: (1) Full name and address of the buyer - To this end, the buyer shall be required to present any acceptable proof of identification; (2) Issue/telephone number of the SIM pack; and (3) Value/amount ofthe SIM packs. The corporations, partnerships and single proprietorships shall also issue proper receipts to the buyers of SIM packs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE TAXING AND OTHER REVENUE-RAISING POWERS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This measure seeks to AMEND RA 7160, the Local Government Code, in order to EXPAND taxing/revenue- raising power of LGUs.  It proposes (1) a general definition of "AMUSEMENT PLACES" to cover all types of amusement places; and (2) to allow provincesto impose a tax on businesses enjoying a FRANCHISE, whether national, legislative or local in nature.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF CHAPTER 2, TITLE THREE, BOOK II OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The allocation of more resources to local government units is one of the most significant imports of the Code which gives a wider space in decision-making and grow in the manner it envisions for itself in consonance with its potentials and capabilities. The just share of local government units in the national wealth, among others, allow them to respond to the demands of local governance.> As a key feature, the bill, therefore, seeks to amend the sharing scheme of the national wealthvis-a-vis the local government unit's share which is of paramount importance, considering the enormous task of meeting the various need of their respective constituencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RE-ALLOCATION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to AMEND Section 285 of the Local Government Code of 1991 as follows:> The shares of local government units in the internal revenue allotment shall, STARTING IN 1999, be allocated AFTER DEDUCTING THEREFROM THE COST OF THE DEVOLVED FUNCTIONS AND PERSONNEL, INCLUDING PERSONNEL HIRED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BEFORE DECEMBER 1991 TO PERFORM THE DEVOLVED FUNCTIONS, AND THE COST OF THE CITY-FUNDED HOSPITALS AND LEGISLATED BENEFITS, EXCLUDING CAPITAL OUTLAYS.  THE TOTAL COST SO DEDUCTED SHALL BE DISTRIBUTED AND REMITTED DIRECTLY TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS CONCERNED AND THE NET BALANCE OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT SHALL BE ALLOCATED in the following manner: "(a) Provinces - Twenty-three percent (23%) "(b)  Cities - Twenty--three percent (23%) "(c) Municipalities - Twenty-four percenct (24%) "(d) Barangays - Twenty percent (20%) Provided, however, That the share of each province, city and municipality shall be determined on the basis of the following formula: "(a) Popu
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING R.A. NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE, GIVING MUNICIPALITIES MORE EQUITABLE SHARE OF NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Local Government Code of 1991 (Section 287) is amended to read as follows: Each local goverment units shall appropriate in its annual basic budget [no less than twenty percent (20%)] A CERTAIN PERCENTAGE of its annual internal revenue allotmentfor development projects IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING SCHEDULE: "WHEN INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT IS LESS THAN P100,000.00 --- TWENTY PERCENT (20%) MORE THAN P100,000.00 BUT      LESS THAN P200,000.00 --- TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) MORE THAN P200,000.00 BUT      LESS THAN P300,000.00 --- THIRTY PERCENT (30%) MORE THAN P300,000.00 --- THIRTY-FIVE PERCENT (35%)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE SCHEDULE OF FAIR MARKET VALUES OF REAL PROPERTY SHALL BE PREPARED BY THE LOCAL ASSESSMENT COUNCIL AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Before any general revision of property assessment is made pursuant to the provision of this Title, there shall be prepared a schedule of fair market values by the [provincial , city and the municipal assessors] LOCAL ASSESSMENT COUNCIL OF EACH PROVINCE CITY OR MUNICIPALITY [the municipalities within Metropolitan Manila Area] for the different classes of real property situated in their respective local governent units for enactment by ordinance of the sanggunian concerned. The schedule of fairmarket values shall be posted in the provincial capitol city or municipal hall and in two other conspicuous public places therein. > THE LOCAL ASSESSMENT COUNCIL SHALL BE COMPOSED OF THE PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICER, ASSESSOR, A REPRESENTATIVE FRROM THE SANGGUNIAN AND A REPRESENTATIVE FROM THE PRICATE SECTOR OR NON-GOVERNMENTA L ORGANZIATIONS REPRESENTED IN THE LOCAL DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE CENTER FOR LEADING-EDGE EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGIES, PROVIDING FOR ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Charter of the Center for Leading-Edge Educational Techniques." This bill seeks the establishment of a Center for Leading-Edge Educational Technologies (CLET) which will bring together the academic, technological and economic forces that, only in consort, can advance the educational promise of affordable materials for use in these emerging technologies. To be able to do this, we need to train people to be CLET experts and acquire a critical mass of equipment and software, centrally located inhigh-technology facility.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-09-08

first_reading.comm_act: chamge of ctte. ref'ls from Basic Ed;Higher Ed and Ways and Means as per Rules Instructio n on 7/25/

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM TAXATION ALL DONATIONS, GRANTS OR GIFTS TO NON-STOCK AND NON-PROFIT EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract: Any provision of law to the contrary, all monetary contributions and the equivalent monetary value of properties donated, granted or bestowed to non-stock and non-profit educational institutions are tax-exempt and deductible from the taxable incomeof the donor. Provided, that such donations, grants, endowments or contributions shall be used actually, directly and exclusively for the primary educational purposes of the recipient. Provided, further, that not more thab twenty-five percent (25%) of the donations, grants, endowments or contributions shall be used for administrative purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A SPECIAL BASIC EDUCATION FUND, PROVIDING FOR A MECHANISM FOR ITS ADMINISTRATION AND SOURCES OF FUNDING INCLUDING THE IMPOSITION OF ADDITIONAL CHARGES AND TAXES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: To provide assistance to basic education, this bill proposes the cretion of a Special Basic Education Fund that shall be exclusively spent to improve and maintain the quality of basic education. The fund shall be in addition to the existing Special Education Fund provided for under R.A. No. 5447 which was created as a financial support to education as a whole.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ALL OBJECTS OF UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE IN PHILIPPINE WATERS
rows.abstract: This bill aims to protect and preserve our underwater cultural heritage by providing for general requirements for underwater archaeology, exploration, and excavation, the description of the items to be protected, prohibition of certain activities inthe vicinity of a protected item and site, the establishment of a reward system for verified reports, and the imposition of sanction/penalt ies for violations.

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE PUBLIC ATTORNEY'S OFFICE (PAO), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987
rows.abstract: THE PUBLIC ATTORNEY'S OFFICE SHALL BE PLACED UNDER THE ADMINISTRATIVE SUPERVISION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE.> IT SHALL INDEPENDENTLY DISCHARGE ITS MANDATE TO RENDER FREE OF CHARGE, LEGAL REPRESENTATION ASSISTANCE, AND COUNSELING TO INDIGENT PERSONS IN ADMINISTRATIVE, LABOR, CIVIL AND CRIMINAL CASES AFTER IT IS DETERMINED THAT THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE WILL BE SERVED THEREBY.> IN THE EXIGENCY OF SERVICE, THE PAO MAY BE CALLED UPON BY PROPER AUTHORITIES TO RENDER SUCH SERVICES TO OTHER PERSONS,SUBJECT TO EXISTING LAWS, RULES AND REGULATIONS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANNER OF REMOVAL OF THE PRESIDING JUSTICE AND ASSOCIATE JUSTICES OF THE SANDIGANBAYAN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1606, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The Presding Justice and the Associate Justice shall [not be remived from office except on impeachment upon the grounds and in the manner provided for in Section 2, 3 and 4 Article XIII of the 1973 Constitution] BE SUBJECT TO THE DISCIPLINARY POWEROF THE SUPREME COURT AND MAY BE REMOVED FROM OFFICE IN THE MANNER PROVIDED FOR IN SECTION 11 OF ARTICLE VIII OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF FORENSIC MEDICINE UNDER THE PHILIPPINE GENERAL HOSPITAL, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to establish a Department of Forensic Medicine under the government-run Philippine General Hospital for the purpose of providing impartial and unbiased scientific and technical investigative services to an accused in a criminal case or to any private interested party.  It also aims to upgrade crime laboratory facilities in the country in order to improve the examination of physical evidence involved in crimes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OF PERSONS ARRESTED, ACCUSED OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION IN A DEGRADING MANNER, AND AMENDING FOR SUCH PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7438, ENTITLED "AN ACT DEFINING CERTAIN RIGHTS OF PERSONS ARRESTED, DETAINED ORUNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION AS WELL AS THE DUTIES OF THE ARRESTING, DETAINING, AND INVESTIGATING OFFICERS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF"
rows.title_short: Prohibiting Public Display of Arrested Persons Under Custodial Investigation in a Degrading Manner
rows.abstract: NO PERSON ARRESTED, DETAINED OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION SHALL BE PUT ON PUBLIC DISPLAY IN HAND CUFFS, WITH NAME TAGS OR OTHER TUGS, OR IN ANY MANNER CAUSING OR TENDING TO CAUSE DEGRADATION, HUMILIATION, DISHONOR, DISCREDIT, RIDICULE OR CONTEMPT, NOT SHALL SUCH PERSON BE PRESENTED TO THE PRESS IN SUCH MANNER. SUBJECT TO THE PRECEDING RESTRICTIONS, THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OR PRESENTATION TO THE PRESS OF ANY PERSON ARRESTED, ACCUSED, DETAINED, OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION SHALL ONLY BE ALLOWED IF SUCH PERSON IS ASSISTTED BY COUNSEL OF HIS CHOICE DURING THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OR PRESENTATION.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2001-12-19, transmitted to on 2002-01-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-01-02

second_reading.remarks: Considered the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE TAX SCHEME FOR MANUFACTURERS, PRODUCERS OF GOODS, ASSEMBLERS AND PROVIDERS OF SERVICES
rows.abstract: This measure is designed to rationalizE the tax burdens imposed by different tax laws which affect Philippine businesses. It sets a maximum ceiling of 50% of Gross Sales as the maximum amount tax a business has to pay the National Government every fiscal year.  It provides a disciplinary mechanism on taxation by which the competitiveness of local enterprises is preserved and at the same time allowing for reasonable revenue collection.> It provides a starting point for the bonafide rationalization of the whole taxation system towards the end of a strong, vibrant, and competitive economy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING AN ALTERNATIVE MODE OF TAX PAYMENT BY CORPORATIONS, AMENDING FOR SUCH PURPOSE SECTION 56 (A) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO SPUR THE PLANTING OF A BILLION TREES THROUGH COMPLEMENTARY TREE PLANTING PROGRAMS OF THE DENR AND VARIOUS GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND COMMUNITIES, SCHOOLS AND UNIVERSITIES, AND CIVIC AND NON-GOVERNMENTA L ORGANIZATIONS,PROTECTING THE REMAINING NATURAL FORESTS AND FOREST PLANTATIONS, AND CREATING A FUND THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Billion Trees Act of 2001." All sectors of society will be mobilized for this tree planting, particularly national government agencies, the upland, lowland, and coastal communities, LGUs, NGOs, private landowners and corporations, and indigenous peoples. At least one million hectares of open and denuded public forest lands, private lands, and idle portions of alienable and disposable lands will be planted with forest and fruit tree species for the first five years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05812

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO MODERNIZE, STANDARDIZE, REGULATE AND ENHANCE THE PROCUREMENT, FUNCTIONS AND ACTIVITIES OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND INSTRUMENTALITI ES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Public Sector Procurement Reform Act of 2001." Rationale: It is the policy of the Philippine government to ensure that transparency and equal opportunity for all prospective bidders characterize public procurement process. These are important towards ensuring that public procurement is an efficient and effictive process. Unfortunately, different and sometimes conflicting laws, rules and regulations characterize the country's public procurement. > The presence of these problems in the procurement process can be readily addressed with a legislation that will remove conflicts and arbitrariness in  existing procurement laws and rules and regulations. There is a need to shift the procurement emphasis from pre-qualificati on to simple eligibiliity screening and post qualification, using transparent and non-discretiona ry criteria. This will allow for more bidders, lowered government costs and reduced procurement time by as much as six months.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04809

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DETER AND ELIMINATE THE TRAFFICKING OF PERSONS, ESPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS, ESTABLISHING THE NECESSARY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION AND SUPPORT OF VICTIMS OF TRAFFICKING, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Trafficki ng of Persons Act of 2001." The State shall give highest priotrity to the enactment of measures and development of programs that will promote human dignity. Persons especially women and minors shall be afforded protection against violence and exploitation, and definite measures will be taken to eliminate the trafficking in persons especially women and minors. > It shall likewise, be the policy of the State to promote an active and visible policy of mainstreaming gender perspective in all efforts aimed at addressing the attendant issues to migration and violence against persons especially women and minors. > Special recognition is given to the vulnerability of women and minors and it shall afford special protection to them.>> Specific measures will be instituted, not only to support trafficked persons especially women and minors, but more importantly, to mitigate pressures for involuntary migration and servitude of persons especially women and minors.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A NATIONAL LAND USE CODE, PROVIDING IMPLEMENTING MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The country has NO Land Use Code that will serve as a sustainable growth map for both public and private investors. A land use code is necessary for targeting and delineating areas open for investment in line with the country's development plans.  There is a need for certain lands to be set aside to establish "agricultural reserves" for food security. It will also help resolve conflicts arising from various economic uses of lands versis the housing needs of the population.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Because of the ralatively large amount of details and particulars of any proposed government regoranization, there is a strong clamor for a transparent, well-studied and comprehensive plan. The proposed bill provides for a multi-year program of bureaucratic re-engineering to allow for thorough study and public consultations (which agencies and government functions are vital and necessary and which ones are not). rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROVIDENT PERSONAL SAVINGS PLAN KNOWN AS THE "PERSONAL EQUITY AND RETIREMENT ACCOUNT"(PERA)
rows.abstract: The bill provides that contributions made to PERA per taxable year shall be 100% deductible from the taxable income of the contributor, subject to certain conditions. This aims to encourage more people to invest their money in PERA. > Through PERA,Filipinos can prepare for and enjoy their retirement years.  They are assured of a financially secure future. The bill will also facilitate an increase in savings because funds deposited to the PERA can be invested in securities including ordinary shares of stock. It will also offer facilities to move funds to high investment levels and take advantage of prevailing market conditions. This means more funds will be available for investments to spur economic growth.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06001

rows.abstract: The bill provides for the strengthening of financial assistance programs for local shipowners. Incentives for the development of private ports through Build-Operate Transfer schemes are also provided for.  This will encourage further private sectorparticipation in the shipping industry.> The bill hopes to hasten investment into the shipping sector, increase domestic fleet, improve service and outreach, reduce sea transport rates and push the country on the path to faster growth.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE CABLE TELEVISION INDUSTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING IMPLEMENTING MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: At present cable TV is classified under the broadcast industry although some sectors claim that it belongs to the telecommunicati ons sector. But cable TV can neither be classified as public utility or media. It can not be considered public utility because its facilities are used more as support structures to complement the transport system of telecommunictio ns, If the definition of media is to be strictly followed. it can not be also classified as such. Media are means of communication with wide range of influence while cable TV covers only a limited number of users who pay for the service. > The proposed bill on cable TV tries to resolve this issue by recognizing it as a SEPARATE and DISTINCT industry meant to supplement andcomplement the telecommunicati ons and broadcast sectors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE THE INTERCONNECTION BETWEEN AND AMONG PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATI ONS ENTITIES, PROVIDING FOR POLICIES AIMED AT RESOLVING INTERCONNECTION DISPUTES AND THE IMPLEMENTING MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (CONVERGENCE)
rows.abstract: The bill provides punishment for refusal or failure of any telecommunicati ons entity to comply with interconnection regulations after having been required by lawful written order of the National Telecommunicati ons Commission (NTC). Acts such as willful termination, disconnection, discontinuity, interruption, blocking and/or disruption of interconnection by any public telecommunicati ons entity will be prohibited. > Procedures for interconnection and reconnection and matters to be covered in the interconnection agreement will be provided for. The parameter for interconnection including points of interconnection , quantity of interconnection circuits, underwriting interconnection costs and interconnection costs will also be laid out. Crimiinal penalties for the violation of such will be provided for.

rows.title_full: AN ACT POSTPONING THE BARANGAY ELECTIONS AND REALIGNING THE APPROPRIATIONS OF THE BARANGAY ELECTIONS FOR THE COMPUTERIZATION OF THE NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The regular elections for punong barangay, sangguniang barangay members, and the sangguniang kabataan chairman shall be POSTPONED to secondy Monday of May 2005. Thereafter, regular elections for barangay officials shall be held every five years.  The incumbent punong barangay, sangguniang barangay members and sangguniang kabataan chairman shall continue in office in a hold-over capacity until their successors shall have been duly elected and qualified in the next regular elections.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04456
